correctness.rationale: Every member of S compares d_S(i)/|S| with 2/n, giving n*d_S(i)>2|S|; a nonempty proper subset with minimum induced degree two cannot occur in a cycle. For smaller-than-half sets, strict blocking is equivalent to no singleton 1-runs, counted by n/r times a product of two composition binomials. Transfer matrix M(z) has characteristic F(lambda,z)=lambda(lambda-1)(lambda-z)-z^2; at z=3/4 its Perron root is 3/2, the logarithmic mean is 1/2 and variance 1/3. Self-loops with different weights ensure strong aperiodicity, proving the local Gaussian coefficient law. Geometric tail summation produces the exact parity constants. Extractable exact verifier passed 16 independent direct-subset cases and 148 matrix-vs-run cases. Finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Fioravanti et al. 2023 introduce the uniform blocking fraction and provide general subexponential-in-n sufficient guarantees but do not enumerate blocking sets or compute the exact parity-sensitive decay for the grand partition of unweighted cycles. Aziz et al. identify a five-cycle strict-core obstruction but no all-n probability. Fanelli et al. 2021 and Demeulemeester–Peters 2024 analyze size- and multiplicative-improvement relaxations, not random-deviation mass. Prior mathematical findings on K_{a,b} block counts, K_{a,2} minimum blockers and a different cyclic social-distance utility do not imply this result. Cyclic run counting and matrix techniques themselves are not claimed to be new; priority uncertainty is explicit.
residual_risks: Automata enumeration of cyclic binary strings without isolated runs may appear in earlier combinatorial literature; the pure enumerative method is not claimed as novel.
Unindexed specialist results on probabilistic blocking frequency in simple fractional hedonic graphs may exist.
Only the specified grand-coalition partition is analyzed. Other cycle partitions can be core stable, so no global optimal epsilon claim is made.

value.rationale: The uniform random blocking probability is precisely the epsilon-fractional core stability statistic studied in the 2023 motivating work. The canonical grand coalition is core-unstable for all cycle sizes at least five, yet has an explicit exponentially small random-deviation risk with a sharp rate sqrt(3)/2, polynomial n^{-1/2} factor and an even/odd boundary effect. The result makes a natural network-baseline risk quantitatively precise instead of merely certifying existence or nonexistence of a blocking coalition. It is not a claim about optimality among partitions.
